The Client 

Tacobar Seaford is a popular Mexican restaurant in Seaford, Victoria. They are looking to hire a full-time Chef to join their passionate kitchen team.  


The Role 

You will have the opportunity to work at an established business which will develop you professionally and to allow you to hone your skills and techniques even further. You will also have opportunities to progress in the business and play an important role in the continued success of the restaurant. 

This is a full time role with an annual salary set at $80,000 plus superannuation. 

 


Responsibilities 

Costing menu items including costing of food and labour costs 

Plan, collect, estimate food and commodities for menus 

Skills in a wide range of cookery methods to produce a range of menu items 

Plan and sequence the timing of food and preparation of tasks 

Evaluate food products to ensure quality standards are consistently attained 

Being responsible for examining, tasting and improving all food prepared to ensure quality 

Following guidelines and regulating quantities of all herbs and spices and cooking times to ensure consistency in all Authentic recipes 

Considering instructions related to preparing orders to meet special dietary requirements 

Work to resolving kitchen related issues, listen to feedbacks and seek solutions in conjunction with fellow staff 

Help enforcing general cleanliness and maintenance of the Kitchen area. 

Working closely with the kitchen staff, the head chef and the restaurant attendants in crafting newer, unique food items and finalising its parameters 

Whilst cooking, ensure proper and adequate seasoning of all food that is served in the restaurant. 

Knowledge of supplies, equipment and services, ordering and inventory control. 

May select and train kitchen staff. 

Leading the kitchen team 

Advise and demonstrate on portioning of ingredients and food, placing it on plates, dressing and garnishes 

Ensure all inventory and the general keeping of the Cold Room and also advise accordingly on storing food in temperature-controlled facilities 

 

 

 

Requirements 

To be successful in this role, you must have:s 

Relevant Certificate 3 or 4 qualifications in commercial cookery  

Minimum 12 months of experience as a Chef 

Must have at least 12 months of experience in cooking over grill 

At least 12 months experience in protein marination, spice rubs, grilling, braising, slow cooking, searing, frying, slicing, and portion control 

At least s12 months experience preparing tacos, tortillas, salsas, guacamole, beans, rice, pickled garnishes, sauces, and layered fillings 

At least 12 months experience managing mise en place, batch preparation, holding temperatures, prep lists, service sequencing, and rapid order execution 

At least 12 months of menu planning experience, and know how to csreate new recipes and design menu according to budget 

Knowledge and experience in modern Mexican cuisine is essential 

Must know how to work with dietary requirements such as vegan, and gluten free food preparation techniques 

Must be able to work with variety of proteins including beef, pork, seafood 

Experience in adherence to recipe & portion control, as well as ordering and stock control 

Ability to follow instruction & take direction 

Excellent time management and attention to detail 

Knowledge of food safety and hygiene standards 

Excellent communication skills and the ability to work as part of a team 

Be available to work on weekends to deal with many customers

result.description:
Graduate Accountant
Specialised Breeders Australia Pty Ltd
Bagshot, Victoria  |  Full-Time  |  $79,423 – $90,000 per annum
About Us
Specialised Breeders Australia Pty Ltd is a leading name in the poultry breeding industry, committed to operational excellence and sustainable production. We are seeking a motivated Graduate Accountant to join our finance team and support the financial operations of our growing business.
This is an excellent opportunity for accounting professional to gain broad exposure to financial and management accounting within a dynamic agribusiness environment, while working closely with senior finance leadership including the Financial Accountant, Management Accountant, Purchasing supervisor and CFO. 
About the Role
Reporting to the Financial Accountant, the Graduate Accountant will play a key role in accounts processing, statutory compliance, cost analysis and month-end reporting. This role offers genuine variety and the chance to build a strong foundation across all areas of financial accounting.
Key Duties and Responsibilities
•	Preparing and lodging monthly Business Activity Statements (BAS) and PAYG obligations in compliance with ATO requirements.
•	Preparing and submitting Chick Hatching and Egg Promotion Levy Returns in accordance with DAFF requirements and maintaining supporting accounting records.
•	Processing supplier invoices, creditor payments and foreign currency transactions through the ERP and banking systems.
•	Allocating and reconciling daily customer receipts and investigating payment discrepancies as they arise.
•	Undertaking company banking, monthly bank reconciliations and supporting schedules for financial reporting.
•	Preparing monthly and quarterly costing and variance reports for biological assets, production inputs, labour hire, utilities and operational expenses.
•	Assisting with month-end accounting, accruals, fixed asset register maintenance and audit support (interim and year-end).
•	Preparing employee-related statutory schedules, including PAYG withholding, Payroll Tax, Superannuation, Child Support and FBT obligations.
•	Maintaining and improving ERP accounting processes, internal controls and financial record-keeping systems.
•	Liaising with external stakeholders, including auditors, financial institutions and taxation authorities, as well as internal managers and stakeholders.
•	Coordinating with purchasing coordinators and operations managers to prepare monthly creditor and electricity accrual journals for review by the Financial Accountant.
•	Monitoring and analysing biological asset operating costs, expenditure trends and profitability, and reporting findings for month-end financial reporting.
•	Supporting the Financial Accountant with fixed asset additions, disposals and reconciliations, along with other ad-hoc accounting duties.
•	Providing financial and accounting support to managers and stakeholders, including advice on accounting procedures, cost control and reporting requirements.
•	Attending to general finance administration and responding to finance-related enquiries from internal stakeholders.
Qualifications and Experience
•	Minimum Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a closely related discipline.
•	Minimum two (2) year of relevant professional accounting experience.
•	Sound knowledge of accounting principles, financial reporting and taxation compliance.
•	Strong analytical, organisational and communication skills.
•	Working towards CA/CPA qualification is preferred. 
What We Offer
•	Competitive salary of $79,423– $90,000 per annum.
•	Mentoring and support provided towards CA/CPA qualification
•	Opportunity to gain exposure across other areas of the finance function.
•	Supportive team environment within a well-established agribusiness.
How to Apply
Click Apply Now to submit your resume and a cover letter outlining your suitability for the role.
Specialised Breeders Australia Pty Ltd is an equal opportunity employer.

Location: 		Griffin, QLD, 4503
Full-Time: 		Immediate start
Reports to:		Facility Manager
Job Title: 		Residential Care Officer
Salary range: 		$79,500 - $85,000 - depending on skills level and work experience + superannuation.
Job Closure date:	30 days

About the Role
On behalf of our client, a dedicated NDIS support service provider with offices across Queensland and New South Wales, we are seeking a compassionate Residential Care Officer. Our client specializes in delivering person-centred support to individuals with disabilities, focusing on fostering independence, community participation, and quality of life. With head office in Hervey Bay and regional offices spanning from Coffs Harbour to Mackay, they are committed to providing friendly, accessible, and tailored care. We are looking for an officer who will uphold these values by delivering high-quality residential support that empowers clients to live well in their own homes or group accommodations.

Key Duties (paraphrased & detailed)
Documentation & Care Planning
• Maintain accurate, current resident documentation including daily progress notes, thorough care assessments, and individualised NDIS-aligned care plans.
• Monitor and meticulously record any changes in residents' physical, emotional, or behavioural needs, promptly reporting concerns to the clinical team.

Personal Care & Independence
• Encourage residents' independence by respectfully assisting with personal care tasks (dressing, grooming, hygiene) in line with their individual care plan.
• Provide consistently high standards of care and support, helping residents build daily living skills and participate in community activities.

Household & Environmental Duties
• Make residents' beds, ensure fresh clean linen is always available, and keep residents' clothing stored neatly and organised.
• Correctly return laundered clothing to appropriate residents' rooms, maintaining a clean, safe, and homely environment.

Meal & Nursing Support
• Assist with meal service, supporting residents during mealtimes with feeding, social engagement, and dietary encouragement as needed.
• Help deliver specialised nursing care under supervision (e.g., medication prompts, mobility assistance), following individual care plans and NDIS Practice Standards.

Communication & Collaboration
• Communicate effectively with colleagues, residents, families, GPs, and allied health professionals to ensure prompt, courteous, and coordinated service delivery.
• Build and nurture positive working relationships with the wider care team, stakeholders, and community groups across multiple office locations.

Rights, Compliance & Safety
• Uphold residents' rights to privacy, confidentiality, choice, and decision-making always, supporting compliance with NDIS standards and company policies.
• Recognise and report potential risks or complaints, follow all OH&S policies, and take responsibility for maintaining a safe environment for yourself, team, and residents.
• Attend team meetings, training sessions, identify personal training needs, contribute to continuous improvement, and champion Equal Employment Opportunity principles.

Skills & Experience Required
• Minimum 1 year full-time relevant experience (disability or community care setting).
• Diploma or relevant qualification in Individual Support, Community Services, or Disability.
• Satisfactory police check, valid driver's license, and own reliable transport.
• Up-to-date annual flu vaccination and full COVID-19 immunization.
• Signed statutory declaration disclosing any serious overseas criminal history (if applicable).
• Current NDIS Worker Screening Clearance (within 5 years) – preferable.
• Genuine team player with a commitment to long-term employment.

Why Join?
Rewarding work making a real difference, ongoing training, supportive team culture, modern facilities, and career growth potential across multiple Queensland and NSW locations.

Please note: We are acting as recruitment agents on behalf of our client. Employer details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.

result.description:
Location: Palmerston, Northern Territory
Employment type: Full-time
Hours: 38 hours per week
Salary: $67,510 to $70,000 plus superannuation

About us
Skills and Hands NT Pty Ltd is a Northern Territory-based consultancy focused on workforce planning, talent engagement, and sustainable staffing strategies. We work alongside local businesses to support the development of strong, reliable teams through tailored pathways that align with their long-term goals. Our role is to facilitate practical workforce solutions that help employers attract and retain skilled talent—contributing to the resilience and continuity of operations across the Territory.

About the business
The business (ABN 91 213 951 452) is a takeaway food outlet located in a busy shopping centre food court in Palmerston. They serve a range of freshly prepared takeaway products, including loaded chips, fish and chips, fried chicken, seafood baskets, hotdogs, ice cream and milkshakes.

They are seeking a reliable and hardworking Kitchenhand to support their food preparation and service team.

About the Role
The Kitchenhand will assist with basic food preparation, maintain clean and hygienic kitchen and service areas, wash utensils and equipment, receive supplies and support the preparation and service of takeaway food.

The position involves standing for extended periods, working in a fast-paced environment and safely handling kitchen equipment, cleaning products and food supplies.

The successful applicant must be available across a rotating roster, including weekends, public holidays and evening shifts where required.

Key Responsibilities
- Clean kitchen, food-preparation, storage and service areas. 
- Wash and sanitise cooking equipment, utensils, containers and other kitchen items.
- Assist with preparing ingredients for cooking and service.
- Portion, assemble and pack food items for customer orders.
- Assist with preparing simple menu items under direction.
- Cook, toast or heat simple food items in accordance with workplace procedures.
- Prepare takeaway packaging, food trays and service materials.
- Receive, transfer, weigh, check and correctly store food supplies.
- Rotate stock and assist with monitoring expiry dates and stock levels.
- Dispose of waste, clean bins and maintain waste-storage areas.
- Maintain clean floors, benches, sinks, fryers and other work areas.
- Assist kitchen and counter staff during busy service periods.
- Follow food-safety, allergen, hygiene and workplace health and safety procedures.
- Report equipment faults, stock shortages and safety issues to the supervisor.
- Complete opening, closing and cleaning duties as allocated.

Skills and Experience
The successful applicant must have:
- Previous experience as a Kitchenhand, food-preparation assistant or in a similar takeaway, hospitality or food-service role;
- Knowledge of basic kitchen hygiene and food-safety practices;
- The ability to follow instructions and workplace procedures;
- The ability to safely use cleaning products and basic kitchen equipment;
- Good attention to cleanliness and food-handling requirements;
- The physical capacity to stand for extended periods and perform repetitive manual duties;
The ability to work efficiently during busy service periods;
Good teamwork and communication skills;
A reliable and punctual approach to work; and
Availability to work weekends, public holidays and shifts according to the business roster.
A food-handling or food-safety certificate is desirable. Relevant workplace training may be provided.
How to Apply
To apply, submit the following:

Resume outlining your work experience and references.
A short cover letter (max. 300 words) explaining:
Why you are applying for this position; and
An example of when you showed excellent service, initiative, or teamwork (use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result).
A Written Response (max. 600 words) describing how your skills and experience align with the responsibilities of the role you are applying for. Please structure your example(s) using the STAR method.
* Only complete applications that address all three components will be considered. Incomplete or generic submissions will not be shortlisted.

If you are interested in joining a busy and growing takeaway food business serving the Palmerston community, we look forward to receiving your application.

Apply online only. Walk-in or telephone enquiries regarding this vacancy will not be accepted.

Applications close: 20 August 2026
